why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repository facts. `npm test` maps to the existing script `node --test`, and test/config.test.js exists. The Check 1 one-liner is valid as written. The JS inside double quotes uses only single quotes, with no `$` or backticks for the shell to expand. The node:fs, node:os and node:path imports are correct. The relative import './src/config.js' resolves from the repository root when run with --eval. The files it names (src/config.js, src/app.js, README.md, test/config.test.js) are all tracked. The builder's steps only edit existing files and run `npm test`. The weakest spots are in the verifier's advisory notes. The valid-JSON check is described in words, not given as a literal command; pasting '{"port": 9000}' straight into the double-quoted script would need its quotes escaped. `node src/app.js <bad-file>` uses a placeholder. Both are advisory and not pass/fail, so no required command breaks.
